title: Monthly Housing Allowance Terms Under Education Benefits, All Tiers
content:
Under Education Benefits (GI Bill and Dependents' Education), a monthly housing allowance is paid to the student only on the Post-9/11 GI Bill (Chapter 33) levels. The terms below fix, tier by tier, whether housing is paid, the rate of pursuit a term must exceed, how the rate of pursuit is rounded for housing, the monthly figures used for distance learning and foreign schools, the length of a full month for proration, and whether payments continue between terms.

| Tier | Housing allowance paid to the student | Rate of pursuit that must be exceeded | Rounding of the rate of pursuit for housing | Monthly figure, distance learning only (before benefit level and rate of pursuit) | Monthly figure, foreign school (before benefit level and rate of pursuit) | Days treated as a full month | Payments continue between terms |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Montgomery GI Bill - Selected Reserve (Chapter 1606) | No | 50 percent | Nearest tenth | $0.00 | $0.00 | 30 | No |
| Survivors' and Dependents' Educational Assistance (Chapter 35) | No | 50 percent | Nearest tenth | $0.00 | $0.00 | 30 | No |
| Montgomery GI Bill - Active Duty (Chapter 30) | No | 50 percent | Nearest tenth | $0.00 | $0.00 | 30 | No |
| Post-9/11 GI Bill (Chapter 33) - 60% Benefit Level | Yes | 50 percent | Nearest tenth | $1169.00 | $2338.00 | 30 | No |
| Post-9/11 GI Bill (Chapter 33) - 70% Benefit Level | Yes | 50 percent | Nearest tenth | $1169.00 | $2338.00 | 30 | No |
| Post-9/11 GI Bill (Chapter 33) - 80% Benefit Level | Yes | 50 percent | Nearest tenth | $1169.00 | $2338.00 | 30 | No |
| Post-9/11 GI Bill (Chapter 33) - 90% Benefit Level | Yes | 50 percent | Nearest tenth | $1169.00 | $2338.00 | 30 | No |
| Post-9/11 GI Bill (Chapter 33) - 100% Benefit Level | Yes | 50 percent | Nearest tenth | $1169.00 | $2338.00 | 30 | No |

**Notes to the table**

1. The 50 percent figure is a floor that must be *exceeded*: a term at exactly 50 percent rate of pursuit is not above it, while a term at 60 percent is.
2. "Nearest tenth" means the rate of pursuit, expressed as a fraction of full time, is rounded to one decimal place (for example, a hypothetical 67 percent rate of pursuit is used as 0.7).
3. Every month is treated as 30 days long when a housing or monthly payment is prorated, whatever the calendar length of the month.
4. Because no tier continues payments between terms, the days between one term's end and the next term's start carry no housing allowance on any tier.
5. The $1169.00 and $2338.00 figures stand in for the campus housing rate only for a term taken wholly by distance learning or at a foreign school respectively.
